name: Sweden
hook: Nobel, Volvo, Bergman and Queen Christina: Sweden's clues are about its exports and its monarchs.

facts.label: Alfred Nobel
facts.statement: Alfred Nobel was born in Sweden in 1823 and died in San Remo, Italy, in 1896; the company bearing his name is Sweden's largest chemicals maker.

facts.label: Volvo
facts.statement: Volvo built its first car in Gothenburg in 1927, and its Gothenburg headquarters was designed by American architect Romaldo Giurgola.

facts.label: Queen Christina
facts.statement: Queen Christina, the 17th-century Swedish queen, founded what became the University of Helsinki; she converted to Catholicism and is buried in St. Peter's Basilica.

facts.label: Ingmar Bergman
facts.statement: All three of Sweden's Oscars for Best Foreign Language Film went to Ingmar Bergman, whose Cries and Whispers is Viskingar och rop at home.

facts.label: the Gulf of Bothnia
facts.statement: The Gulf of Bothnia, the Baltic's largest arm, separates Sweden from Finland; the Torne River runs along that border into it.

facts.label: Peter the Great
facts.statement: Sweden's Charles XII lost the Great Northern War to Peter the Great, whose victory at Poltava in 1709 spurred the Russian Empire's rise.

facts.label: Helsinki
facts.statement: Gustav I Vasa founded Helsinki in 1550; Finland's largest city moved to its present site in 1640.
